summary: Wheeling Ohio County Airport (HLG/KHLG) is a public general-aviation airport serving Wheeling and West Virginia’s Northern Panhandle from a hilltop site east of the city. It supports private, corporate, and emergency aircraft with paved runways and basic services, but no scheduled commercial airline flights. The field is a convenient reliever and gateway for the Ohio Valley, roughly an hour from Pittsburgh.
faqs:
Q: Does Wheeling Ohio County Airport have commercial passenger flights?
A: No. HLG is a general-aviation airport with no scheduled airline service; passengers typically connect via Pittsburgh International Airport (PIT) or other larger regional airports.

Q: What services are available at KHLG?
A: Expect basic general-aviation services such as fuel, tiedowns, and hangars; availability can vary, so confirm current hours, fuel, and any maintenance or courtesy-car options with the airport or FBO before arrival.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Wheeling?
A: It is about 10–15 miles east/northeast of downtown Wheeling, typically a 15–25 minute drive depending on route and traffic.

Q: What are the airport codes?
A: IATA: HLG; ICAO: KHLG; FAA LID: HLG. The field elevation is approximately 1,194 feet MSL.
transport_tips: A car is the most practical way to get to and from HLG, as the airport sits in a rural area east of Wheeling. From I-70, follow US-40/National Road or local roads; use GPS because signage is limited. Taxi, rideshare, and rental-car availability is limited, so arrange your return ride or rental before you arrive.
local_tip: Because the airport sits on high, hilly terrain, expect variable winds and mechanical turbulence on approach; check the AWOS and plan a stabilized final, especially in summer when density altitude is high.
